generated_by: LabVIEW 2026 driven through its ActiveX server (LabVIEW.Application COM / VI Server)
directory: capture folder on the capture machine
method_that_worked: Method C/D (run existing VI via COM). Shipped, runnable VIs in vi.lib/variable/tagger/mndui/config/gendialog/dataConversion.llb wire a typed front-panel control to LabVIEW's native Flatten-To-String and expose the raw result in the 'data string' indicator. Driven via GetVIReference + SetControlValue + Run + GetControlValue. Output read as a BSTR and decoded with cp1252 (LabVIEW's ANSI<->BSTR codepage on this Spanish Windows); the cp1252 round-trip was proven lossless by byte-matching every reproduced value. Typed input controls discovered per VI: NumToFlattenVariant.vi control 'Numeric' (DBL), BitArrayToFlattenVariant.vi control 'Bit Array' (U32 scalar), BoolToFlattenVariant.vi control 'Boolean', TextToFlattenVariant.vi control 'Text' (String), BLOBToFlattenVariant.vi control 'Text' (String, flattened as a U32-length-prefixed byte/U8 array). Every captured value was byte-verified against its independently-computed expected value.
com_binding_note: On this machine PowerShell's native COM adapter returns a broken dispatch for LabVIEW.Application (Version came back empty, member access threw NullReference). The reliable route is late-bound IDispatch: create the instance with [Activator]::CreateInstance([Type]::GetTypeFromProgID('LabVIEW.Application')) and invoke every member via reflection Type.InvokeMember (GetVIReference needs its 3 optional args passed explicitly, _GetTagNames needs a by-ref ParameterModifier). Strong-typed interop casting also fails: the LabVIEW automation objects expose IDispatch only (QueryInterface for the vtable interfaces returns the null IID), so a tlbimp interop (generated here from resource\labview.tlb to read exact member signatures) is usable for introspection but not for casting the live RCW. GetControlValue/SetControlValue address controls by front-panel label and only accept controls wired into the VI's connector pane.
methods_A_B_result: IMPOSSIBLE. LabVIEW VI Scripting is not exposed through the ActiveX/VI-Server COM server (no Diagram/Node/Constant classes in the type library; NewVI/OpenVIReference/BlockDiagram and all node-creation names fail GetIDsOfNames on live Application and VI objects). Scripting is only available from inside G, which cannot be bootstrapped headlessly. Diagram authoring was NOT retried in this run (accepted as proven). g-cli is not installed; VI Server over TCP has the same object model.
cross_checks: All captured scalars/strings verified against NI-documented flatten layout and reproduced byte-for-byte from live LabVIEW: DBL 0.25->3fd0000000000000, DBL 1.0->3ff0000000000000, +Inf->7ff0000000000000, -Inf->fff0000000000000, NaN->7ff8000000000000, Bool TRUE->01, FALSE->00, String 'ABC'->00000003414243, empty->00000000 (U32 big-endian length prefix confirms prepend-size default ON and big-endian). New this run: 32-bit integer -19 data string ->ffffffed, U32 19 ->00000013 (4-byte big-endian, no type descriptor), U8/byte array [1,2,3] ->00000003010203 and [255,0,16] ->00000003ff0010 (U32 big-endian count + raw bytes). Every new case byte-matched its independently-computed expected value.

blocked_cases_no_fixture_written.name: 1-D DBL array [1,2,3]
blocked_cases_no_fixture_written.blocker: No shipped, runnable VI on this machine exposes a settable DBL-array (or any typed numeric-array) control wired to the raw Flatten-To-String primitive. The only array-capable clean flatten wrapper found is BLOBToFlattenVariant.vi, whose control is a byte/U8 array (captured separately as flatten_u8_array_*). vi.lib/Utility/VariantFlattenExp.vi has a settable 'variant' control but (a) ignores a COM-set value (SetControlValue does not land on the variant terminal, the flatten always emits the empty-variant form) and (b) flattens in variant format with an embedded type descriptor (30-byte constant), not the clean typed array flatten. method_datalog_2026_10_12: Second capture run (2026-10-12): front-panel datalogging driven over ActiveX. Set the VI properties LogFilePath and LogAtFinish=TRUE, set inputs with SetControlValue, Run, then read the DTLG file LabVIEW writes. Each record holds a U32+U16 header followed by every front-panel control in the flatten encoding; fields were located by walking the type descriptors stored in the same file. Equivalence with Flatten To String was validated in the same run: NumToFlattenVariant.vi (Numeric=0.25) logged Numeric=3fd0000000000000 and its Flatten To String 'data string' indicator contained exactly 3fd0000000000000; TextToFlattenVariant.vi (Text='ABC') logged Text=00000003414243 and its 'data string' contained exactly 00000003414243. Clusters are set over COM as nested object[] (assign with Array.SetValue to avoid PowerShell PSObject wrapping); 2-D arrays as double[,].
ext_verdict: LabVIEW 2026 (Windows x64) flattens EXT as 16 big-endian bytes in IEEE 754 binary128 layout: sign bit, 15-bit exponent with bias 16383, no explicit integer bit, 112-bit fraction. Evidence: 1.0 -> 3fff0000000000000000000000000000 (x87-padded would be 3fff8000000000000000000000000000), 0.1 -> 3ffb999999999999a000000000000000 (the DBL fraction 999999999999a left-aligned; x87 would be 3ffbcccccccccccccd00000000000000), DBL subnormal 1e-310 -> normalized 3bf92688b70e62b00000000000000000. Values entered as DOUBLE via COM, so fraction bits below bit 60 are zero.
